reason: The bone framework has spaces awaiting mineral, so this directly addresses the goal of strengthening the bones.
expectation: The mineral will strengthen the living bone framework.

alternatives.reason: The cells could also begin building a muscle, but strengthening the bones is equally clear.

effect: The mineral strengthened the bones while leaving the joint able to move; the remaining goal is to build the muscles.
reaction: It was useful to see that the joint's soft parts stayed unmineralized.
reason: The front attachments have a space for muscle cells, so placing them there should build one of the two muscles.
expectation: The cells will form a muscle between the front tendon attachments.

alternatives.reason: The back attachments also need a muscle; either side seems like a reasonable place to start.

effect: The front muscle is the biceps, and its pull bends the elbow. The back attachment still needs a muscle.
reaction: The picture makes it clear how the biceps pulls across the joint.
reason: The back attachments have the other space for muscle cells, so they are the next clear place to build.
expectation: The cells will form a muscle behind the elbow that pulls from the opposite side.

effect: The triceps pulls from behind to straighten the elbow, showing how the same kind of muscle cell can produce a different movement because of its attachments.
reaction: Seeing the two muscles pull in opposite directions made their jobs clearer.

mostWorthwhile.text: Building both muscles was most worthwhile because their positions explain bending and straightening the elbow.

leastWorthwhile.text: Adding mineral was clear but less interesting than seeing how the muscles move the joint.

surprise.text: The same kind of muscle cell could help make muscles with opposite effects; the attachments determine the direction of the pull.

arbitrary.text: None of the actions felt arbitrary: the spaces and goals made their purposes clear.

continue.text: I would choose to continue because building the arm helped me connect its parts to movement, and I would be curious to see another body system.
